title: Maximum Value of an Ordered Triplet I
statement:
For three indices `i < j < k` of the integer array `nums`, define their score as `(nums[i] - nums[j]) * nums[k]`.

Return the highest score over all such index triples. If every triple scores below zero, return `0` instead. The answer can exceed the 32-bit range, so the result is a 64-bit integer.
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 100 values, trying every triple `(i, j, k)` is O(n³) and fast enough, but the enumeration can be much leaner. Fix the last index `k`. Since `nums[k]` is positive, the best triple ending at `k` uses the largest difference `nums[i] - nums[j]` with `i < j < k`. That difference, in turn, only needs the largest `nums[i]` before each `j`. Both maxima can be carried forward while enumerating `k` once.

## Approach

1. Start `best`, `maxLeft` and `maxDiff` at `0` (a triple with a negative score never beats `0`).
2. For each `k`, first use `nums[k]` as the third value: try `maxDiff * nums[k]` as a new `best`.
3. Then use `nums[k]` as a middle value: update `maxDiff` with `maxLeft - nums[k]`.
4. Finally use `nums[k]` as a first value: update `maxLeft`.
5. The order matters: each role only sees values from strictly earlier indices. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [12, 6, 1, 2, 7]`.

| `k` | `nums[k]` | `best` | `maxDiff` | `maxLeft` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 12 | 0 | 0 | 12 |
| 1 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 12 |
| 2 | 1 | 6 | 11 | 12 |
| 3 | 2 | 22 | 11 | 12 |
| 4 | 7 | 77 | 11 | 12 |

The answer is `77` = `(12 - 1) * 7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with three constant-time updates per index.
- Space: O(1): three running values.

## Pitfalls

- Update in the order third, middle, first; reversing it lets one index play two roles.
- Return `0` when every score is negative: starting `best` at `0` handles this.
- Scores reach about `10^12`, beyond 32-bit integers; use a 64-bit type in Java or C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | highest score found so far (never below `0`) |
| `maxLeft` | largest value at an index before the current one |
| `maxDiff` | largest `nums[i] - nums[j]` with `i < j` before the current index |
| `k` | the index being processed |

narration.2: No triple counts if every score is negative, so the answer starts at 0.
narration.3: Largest value seen so far, the best candidate for nums[i].
narration.4: Largest nums[i] - nums[j] seen so far, the best first two picks.
narration.5: Enumerate every index once, letting it play each role in turn.
narration.6: As the third index: multiply the best earlier difference by nums[k].
narration.7: As the middle index: subtract nums[k] from the largest earlier value.
narration.8: As the first index: it may become the new largest value.
narration.10: best now holds the highest score over all ordered triples, or 0.
